Feature Development: Take ownership of specific frontend modules and tasks within sprint cycles, driving them from technical design through to production deployment with guidance from senior engineers.

Architecture & Quality: Go the extra mile to surface and implement the right architecture. Write strong test cases, ship clean code, and maintain a high bar for engineering quality.
Product Engineering: Apply a product-minded approach, leveraging engineering spikes and R&D to drive new product improvements and features.
Technical Environment
Core: React, React Fiber (for high-performance rendering)
Integrations: Blender MCP, real-time image/voice streaming
AI Stack: Custom orchestration layer, TTS, ASR, LLMs, prompt engineering tooling
What We’re Looking For
A strong foundation in React and modern frontend engineering (via coursework, personal projects, or previous internships).
A proven ability to dig deep into complex problems, particularly those related to scale and performance.
High standards for code quality, testing, and clean architecture.
Intellectual curiosity about AI infrastructure and a willingness to work hands-on with LLMs, prompt optimization, and adversarial testing.
Who This Opportunity Might Be For
Final-year students looking for an internship + PPO: You are in your final year of college, looking for a high-impact internship that acts as a direct pipeline to a full-time role based on your performance.
3rd-year students looking to intern: You are currently in your 3rd year and have the bandwidth to commit to a 3-month (or longer) internship to gain deep, real-world experience in AI and frontend engineering.
Aspiring frontend engineers ready to become full-stack: You have a strong foundation in frontend development and are eager to expand your scope. You are open to being mentored and actively want to grow into a role that bridges frontend UI with backend AI orchestration layers.
High-ownership builders: You want to drive features end-to-end and be recognized as the owner of your domain.
Engineers with a product mindset: You don't just want to write code; you want to use R&D and technical spikes to directly influence the direction of the product.
Who This Opportunity Might Not Be For To ensure alignment, this role is likely not a fit if:
You prefer strict task execution: If you prefer being handed line-by-line instructions rather than owning specific modules and driving them to completion, this role will not be a good fit.
You just want to "move fast and break things": We move fast, but we are dealing with enterprise and government infrastructure. We value speed, but we value quality, testing, and clean code equally. If you cut corners on tests, you won't enjoy it here.
You are strictly a UI developer: If your focus is exclusively on translating Figma designs to code and you have no interest in diving into the underlying AI orchestration, TTS/ASR layers, or prompt infrastructure, you will find the 30-40% AI requirement unappealing.
You dislike AI operational metrics: If you do not want to engage with the operational challenges of production AI (such as measuring hallucination rates, latency, and running adversarial tests), this scope of work will not suit you.
You prefer low-ambiguity environments: We are a scaling startup dealing with complex, multi-modal AI deployed in government and enterprise environments. If you prefer highly predictable, low-ambiguity work with no operational friction, this environment may be challenging.

Flexible schedule
Provident Fund

Congratulations,
you have taken the first step towards bagging a career-defining role. Join the team of superheroes that safeguard data wherever it goes.
About Seclore:
Seclore is the Data Security Intelligence company for the era of enterprise AI. Seclore helps organisations secure the data that powers how people and AI work, enabling them to adopt AI safely without losing control of sensitive information. By securing data itself and ensuring protection travels with it wherever it moves, Seclore enables trust, control, and resilience across the modern enterprise. Seclore serves more than 500 global enterprises and government organisations across over 40 countries. For more information, visit
www.seclore.com
.
You would love our tribe:
If you are a risk-taker, innovator, and fearless problem solver who loves solving challenges of data security, then this is the place for you!
T H E R O L E
Trainee Product Engineer
Mumbai
Here's what you will get to explore:
You will own problems, not tickets.
The problem is closed when it is actually solved for the customer - not when your part of it is finished.
You will build and ship parts of a security product
that has to behave identically on thousands of machines you will never see, in environments you cannot control, where getting it wrong is not a cosmetic bug.
You will be responsible for whether your work survives contact with reality -
designing how it should be proven, finding the failure before a customer does, and standing behind it once it ships.
You will be handed problems that arrive without a clean description:
a log file, an environment you have never touched, and a customer who is already unhappy. Working out what actually happened is the job.
You will automate anything you have been asked to do more than twice.
We would rather you spent a week building the tool than a year running the process.
You will work across the engineering organisation
rather than inside one corner of it, and you will be expected to hold your own in a technical argument with people far more experienced than you.
You will work the full stack of the product
rather than a slice of it - the interfaces customers touch, the services and APIs behind them, the agents running inside machines in another country, and the operating system and platform layers underneath. Full stack here goes considerably deeper than a web page and a database.
You will get hands-on with how real enterprise software is built and defended -
encryption, platform and OS-level behaviour, enterprise integrations, and the systems Fortune 100 companies actually run on. Very few engineers get this range in their first years, and it is the fastest way we know to build genuine technical judgment.
Candidate Profile:
At Seclore attitude and aptitude trumps everything else. While depth of knowledge is highly valued, we tend to be tech agnostic; what matters most is innovation and working smart.
What we look for, whatever your background:
You learn quickly, and you can point to proof of it.
Tell us about something you did not know six months ago and can do now, and how you got there. Handed an unfamiliar codebase, domain or problem, you make yourself useful early rather than waiting until you feel ready. Half the tooling you will use in three years does not exist yet. Almost everything else on this list can be taught; this one cannot.
You can work out what is actually going on.
You can read code you did not write - most engineering is comprehension before it is creation. And given a symptom, a log file and no direct access, you can reason your way toward what is really happening rather than guessing.
You automate by instinct.
You have built something - a script, a tool, a small utility - because doing the task by hand was not a good use of your time.
You work AI-natively, and you know when not to trust it.
You use AI to write, test, debug and investigate faster than anyone could two years ago, and you can recognise when the output is confidently wrong. Better still if you have gone below the surface - models, embeddings, agents, retrieval, evaluation, and what breaks and why. If you have not yet, what matters is that you want to. We are building AI into products that protect the world's most sensitive information, and that needs people curious about the internals, not only the interface.
You can explain how you got to an answer.
We are more interested in your reasoning than your conclusion. Engineers who can walk through their thinking make better decisions, and they make the people around them better too.
You finish things.
A working, unglamorous, shipped project tells us more than an elegant abandoned one.
You do not draw lines around what counts as your job.
The best engineers we have hired took on whatever the problem required, and got sharper for it.
